admin_cf_description: Creates the DNS records (the panel's too, if it doesn't exist) and requests certificates through DNS-01.
admin_cf_unset_hint: DNS records are created by hand and certificates are requested over HTTP.
admin_cf_note: The token is also kept in Caddy's autosave.
admin_cf_remove_body: Without a token, DNS records are created by hand and certificates are requested over HTTP. To use Cloudflare again you'll have to paste a token again.
admin_cf_modal_description: It needs the Zone:Read and DNS:Edit permissions on the zones it will use. It's stored encrypted and never shown again.
admin_cf_token_hint: muelle checks it with Cloudflare before saving it.
admin_cf_unavailable_body: The token wasn't saved. Paste it again and retry in a moment.
admin_cf_origin_ca_needs_token: Set the Cloudflare token to turn them on.
admin_cf_origin_ca_unavailable: Cloudflare didn't respond: nothing changed. Try again in a moment.
admin_error_cf_token_length: A Cloudflare token has between {min} and {max} characters.
admin_error_cf_token_spaces: No spaces: paste just the token.
admin_ip_description: Where the records muelle creates point to.
admin_ip_v4_hint: Leave it empty and muelle creates no DNS records and leaves the ones it manages alone.
admin_ip_note: Changing it updates the content of the records muelle manages (never their Proxied setting). Removing the IPv6 deletes their AAAA records.
admin_cert_description: Let's Encrypt emails this address if a certificate has problems.
admin_cert_note: The panel domain is set at install time.
admin_ports_description: Where muelle-caddy listens on the host.
admin_ports_warning: Changing them recreates muelle-caddy: sites go down for a few seconds.
admin_ports_confirm_body: muelle-caddy is recreated listening on {http} (HTTP) and {https} (HTTPS). Sites go down for a few seconds.
admin_ports_move_body: Open port {port} in the firewall before confirming: if it's closed you won't be able to reach the panel, and the ports can only be changed back from the server.
admin_ports_applying_body: It can take up to 2 minutes while muelle prepares muelle-caddy.
admin_ports_docker_unavailable: Docker didn't respond on the muelle server while the new ports were being checked. Nothing was saved: try again in a moment.
admin_ports_recreating_title: Recreating muelle-caddy with the new ports…
admin_ports_recreating_body: Sites are back in a few seconds.
admin_ports_recreated: muelle-caddy is listening on the new ports.
admin_ports_recreate_failed_title: muelle-caddy didn't start with the new ports.
admin_ports_recreate_failed_body: {error}. muelle retries on its own with these ports: if one is in use, pick another.
admin_ports_recreate_failed_generic: muelle retries on its own with these ports: if one is in use, pick another.
admin_ports_recreate_unknown_title: Couldn't confirm whether muelle-caddy is listening on the new ports.
admin_ports_recreate_unknown_body: Reload the page in a moment to see how it ended.
admin_ports_rollback_title: muelle went back to the previous ports (HTTP {http}, HTTPS {https}) {when}.
admin_ports_rollback_reason: muelle-caddy didn't start with HTTP {http} and HTTPS {https}: {error}.
admin_ports_rollback_action: Go back to the previous address
admin_ports_moved_body: If you came in through the previous address, it stops responding in a few seconds; your session stays open at the new one. If the new one doesn't respond within a minute, go back to the previous one: if muelle-caddy didn't start on the new port, muelle goes back to the old ports on its own.
admin_ports_moved_body_previous: If you came in through the previous address, it stops responding in a few seconds; your session stays open at the new one. If the new one doesn't respond within a minute, go back to the previous one, {previous}: if muelle-caddy didn't start on the new port, muelle goes back to the old ports on its own.
admin_error_port_same: It must differ from the HTTP one.
admin_security_description: muelle has access to docker.sock: signing in to the panel is the same as being root on the server.
admin_security_2fa_hint: Anyone without it can only set it up when they sign in.
admin_security_totp_first_body: If you require it without having it, you'd be locked in the setup screen.
admin_security_cidrs: IPs allowed to open the panel
admin_security_cidrs_hint: One CIDR range per line. Empty allows any IP.
admin_security_client_ip_out: Your current IP, {ip}, isn't included: saving would lock you out of the panel.
admin_security_lockout_title: You'd lock yourself out of the panel
admin_security_lockout_body: muelle sees this session from {ip}, which isn't on the list. If you save anyway, you'll only get back in from an IP on the list or by clearing it from the server.
admin_security_lockout_body_no_ip: With this list, this session could no longer open the panel. If you save anyway, you'll only get back in from an IP on the list or by clearing it from the server.
admin_error_cidr: Line {line}: “{value}” is neither an IP nor a CIDR range.
admin_registries_description: For private images. The password is stored encrypted.
admin_registries_empty_body: They're only needed to pull private images.
admin_registry_form_description: muelle signs in with these credentials before pulling an image from this host.
admin_registry_form_host_hint: What comes before the image's first /, like ghcr.io. For Docker Hub, docker.io.
admin_registry_form_password_hint_edit: Type it again: the stored one can't be read.
admin_registry_scope_title: They're for all of muelle, not one project
admin_registry_scope_body: Any API token can use them to pull the private images they can see. Use a read-only credential that only sees what you deploy.
admin_registry_delete_body: Deploys that use private images from this host will fail to pull them.
admin_error_registry_host_scheme: No scheme: just the host, like ghcr.io.
admin_error_registry_host_path: Just the host, with no path or trailing /: ghcr.io, not ghcr.io/your-org.
admin_error_registry_host_format: A host like ghcr.io, registry.example.com:5000 or localhost:5000.
admin_error_registry_username_control: No tabs or other control characters.
admin_error_registry_password_newline: No line breaks: paste it on a single line.
admin_error_registry_exists: There's already a registry with that host.
admin_audit_description: 180 days. It never includes variable values.
admin_audit_empty_body: What's done in the panel and through the API shows up here.
admin_audit_load_error: The audit log couldn't be loaded.
admin_error_registry_username_colon: No ":": registry authentication uses it to separate the username from the password.
admin_registry_delete_body_muelle: muelle's images are private and are pulled with this registry: without it, muelle can't pull the Caddy image of a new version, and deploys with private ghcr.io images will fail to pull.
admin_error_placeholder: No curly braces: Caddy reads them as a placeholder and would stop receiving the configuration.
admin_security_recovery_label: To clear it, on the server (restarts muelle for a few seconds):
